rationale: The Latin anchors *balare* and *ovis balat* ("a sheep bleats") confirm the literal, animal-vocal sense of the word. The Old English *blǽtan* denotes the cry of a sheep or lamb, directly matching bleat.v.02 ("cry plaintively," exemplified by "The lambs were bleating"), not the metaphorical/whining human speech sense of bleat.v.01.
